run: bench/egl_probe.py
change: Attempted an offscreen GL context under WSL2 Ubuntu-24.04 to host the planned EGL render path. Two restarts, wsl --update --pre-release, every platform and driver override.

run: bench/readback_probe.py
change: Timed mjr_readPixels per call in isolation at 64x64, then toggled MuJoCo's visual defaults to find the fixed cost. offsamples 4 -> 0, shadowsize 4096 -> 0.
conclusion: MuJoCo discussion #2222's ~30 ms per call does not reproduce - off by three orders of magnitude. The real fixed cost was an MSAA resolve forced by offsamples=4. Two-pass render confirmed with 13x margin, so the WGL pbuffer and the single-pass collapse are both cancelled. Promotes <quality offsamples=0 shadowsize=0/> from cosmetic to a hard arm_blocks.xml requirement.

run: bench/step_probe.py
change: Timed mj_step alone on arm_blocks.xml, idle and driven arms, 5x1000 steps resetting every 200, 6 separate processes. Contact guard narrowed to an arm-block geom-pair filter excluding the table.
conclusion: P-6 is not at risk from physics. Contact counts and both fractions came back bit-identical across 6 processes - unseeded determinism. The earlier ncon>0 guard scored both arms at 100% and was vacuous. E-4's 5% is NOT demonstrated for this number: the series had not plateaued after 6 runs and needs a quiescent-machine protocol.

run: bench/gpu_probe.py
change: Re-measured memory bandwidth and fp16 matmul with the GPU clocked up, in two phases because no single load clocks both domains. Follows a chassis cooling fix.
conclusion: 448 GB/s REFUTED - that figure is the desktop 5060 at 28 Gbps; this Laptop part runs 24, so the ceiling is 384. Every fork-table compute floor rose 45% and CUDA graphs became required on BOTH paths, not just the 144-token one. Cooling alone gave 9x on matmul while every instantaneous throttle flag read Not Active - the evidence was in the PERFORMANCE counters. Also refutes pstate==P0 as a validity gate: pstate follows the memory domain and reads P4 during correct compute-bound work.

run: bench/frame_probe.py
change: Timed the full per-frame generation cost on the real scene - mj_step, mjv_updateScene, two-pass render with the segmentation pass, and readback - 5x1000 calls through the XML 'main' camera.
conclusion: Parallel generation is NOT needed - the trigger does not fire. 300k frames in about a minute single-threaded. mjv_updateScene was the last day-1 unknown and is negligible. p99 exceeds the whole frame budget but P-6 is throughput, not latency, so at 1% weight it costs ~10% of the mean. Taken while the GPU was thermally capped, so this is a pessimistic bound.

run: scene/arm_blocks.xml, first working scene
change: Added a <visual> block with offsamples=0, shadowsize=0 and an ambient-only headlight (diffuse and specular both zero).
conclusion: The ambient-only headlight is what collapses the palette: diffuse light shades per face, so one rgba becomes three entries per box. castshadow=false was listed as the fix and is wrong - it is a <light> attribute and MuJoCo's compiler rejects it on a geom. The contact figure is a full-torque drive, not the 50/50 policy, so it is indicative only.

run: sim/gl_context.cpp
change: Ported the offscreen context to C++20 with four fatal startup checks: renderer deny-list, currentBuffer, viewport against the scene's offwidth/offheight, and mjr_getError. Built /W4 /WX clean in both configurations.
conclusion: F-3 holds from C++, not just from the Python probe. All four checks are fatal at startup, so a software renderer or a silent 640x480 fallback cannot reach the data run. Deny-list on the two software spellings, not an allow-list on 'RTX 5060', which would fail on any other perfectly good machine.

run: sim/policy.cpp, policy_self_check
change: Added the base-3 action encoding and its round-trip self-check. Built /W4 /WX clean in both configurations.
conclusion: All 9 actions decode to distinct ctrl pairs and re-encode to the same index. Gotcha recorded: jnt_qposadr and jnt_dofadr DIVERGE for free joints - block1 is 9 vs 8, block2 16 vs 14, because a free joint is 7 wide in qpos and 6 in qvel. Never compute either address; always read the array.

run: MSVC sanitizer capability check
change: Checked which sanitizers MSVC actually provides, then built and ran under each.
conclusion: E-3 DROPS its UBSan half rather than adding a clang-cl configuration. /fsanitize=undefined and /fsanitize=leak are listed only as possible future work. The one relevant UB class - signed overflow on shard offsets across 3.6 GB - is closed by typing every offset int64_t plus a write-site bounds assert, which runs in the optimised build where a side-configuration sanitizer would not. ASan also needs /Zi (C5072 is fatal under /WX) and its runtime DLL copied beside the binary.

run: policy_dry_run, episode-length A/B
change: A/B on steps_per_episode with steering-off (reach_noise_prob=1.0) as the control that separates 'reach is broken' from 'episode too short'.
conclusion: steps_per_episode=200 REFUTED. 200 steps is 0.4 s of sim time and the arm cannot cross to a block from a random start angle. Changed to 600 x 500 episodes - the same 300k frames - which also cuts ctx=15 boundary loss from 7.5% to 2.5%. The steering-off control gives a 6x separation in median closest approach, so the reach itself works.

run: policy_dry_run, F-5 flatness frontier
change: Swept the Jacobian deadband and per-digit versus whole-action noise across 14 configurations at 200 episodes x 600 steps.
conclusion: F-5's 2.5 ceiling is set at the measured knee, not at a rounder number: arrival is flat at 42.5-44% down to ratio 2.44, then falls off. Per-digit noise dominates whole-action noise at every setting once the deadband is on, and every no-deadband configuration is strictly dominated. Below ~1.7 is unreachable by any tuning - a two-link planar arm reaching outward turns both hinges the same way, which is kinematics. Shipped jacobian_deadband=0.04, reach_digit_noise_prob=0.15.

run: policy_dry_run at F-5's own sample size
change: Ran at the 2,000-episode sample size F-5 actually names, twice, to check both the thresholds and replay.
conclusion: F-5 passes with margin on both thresholds, and the two passes are identical over 1.2M actions. Compliance costs arrival 44% -> 35.7% and median closest 0.042 -> 0.052 m; arrival is a diagnostic, not a requirement. The 200-episode startup smoke run reads ratio 2.30 / min share 6.55% and is marked INDICATIVE - at 200 episodes the ratio moves ~0.2 between samples, which is why F-5 names 2,000.

run: sim/truth.cpp, truth_dry_run
change: Added the segmentation pass and the id-colour decode. Dry run drives actuator 0 at full torque for 1500 steps, with three fatal checks around a teleported block.
conclusion: The id-colour decode r + 256g + 65536b is verified from C++ as well as Python, and identically under both build types, ASan-clean. Both rates are INDICATIVE, not the verdict: the sweep is not the 50/50 policy, and a block punted off the table reads 0 for every remaining frame. New gotcha: the segmentation pass leaves the offscreen framebuffer holding id colours, so the RGB readback MUST precede Truth::read - reversed, the shard stores id colours and nothing downstream fails.

run: scene/arm_blocks.xml, block0 y +0.06 -> -0.06
change: Moved block0 to negative y after it read 0 visible px in the resting pose, which made F-7 score off one static configuration rather than off the arm moving.
conclusion: F-7 now measures the arm passing in front of a block rather than one static pose. Cause: the camera sits at y=-0.5 looking toward +y and the arm rests along +x at y=0, so any block at small positive y is behind it. F-6 is still 10x its floor and F-5's verdict is unchanged. Do not flip the sign back. F-7 keeps one known bias - a block knocked off the table reads zero forever and counts as occluded.

run: sim/shard_writer.cpp, 6-episode generation loop
change: Ran the full generation loop on a small 6-episode config, optimised and under ASan, then read both blobs back in numpy. The config hash for this run was not recorded at the time.
conclusion: ASan-clean. F-4 holds at the PIXEL level - two runs at one seed produced byte-identical .pixels and .meta, which is stronger than policy_dry_run's action-sequence check. The sidecar is absent until commit(), checked at the one moment it is observable. Two decisions came out of it: data_hash is passed in as a required flag and never recomputed in C++, and shards rotate only on episode boundaries because Policy is seeded per shard. The one-shard F-6/F-7 figures here are SUPERSEDED by the full-set gate run below.

run: PHASE 0 GATE - full generation, mirage/configs/base.json
change: Full 300,000-frame generation at base.json, git ce5c193, then a second complete run at the same seed for the replay check.
conclusion: GATE MET, all three conditions: 300k frames on disk, deterministic replay, hardware render confirmed by GL_RENDERER. Replay gave bit-identical .pixels and .meta for all 7 shards - determinism demonstrated over the real dataset, not a sample. data_hash and git_sha identical across all 7 sidecars. CORRECTS a small-sample figure: F-6 and F-7 read 62.4% and 40.3% off a single 1,200-frame shard, 3x the full-set values. Quote the full-set numbers, not those.

run: mirage/data.py + bench/loader_probe.py
change: Added the memmap reader and episode-aware window sampler, then measured loader throughput against P-7's 30-minute epoch budget. Single-threaded, no DataLoader workers.
conclusion: F-8 holds: 448 sampled records decode identically through the structured dtype and through an independent struct.unpack at the documented offsets. Needs NO workers, prefetch or caching layer - 3.43 GiB of pixels in 31.6 GB of RAM means the page cache holds the whole set. Gotcha found by getting it wrong: slicing an np.memmap returns a lazy view and touches no pages, so a first probe reported 3.4M fps having timed slice arithmetic. Row order settled - the blob is bottom-up and the flip belongs in the sampler, not in Shard.pixels. Split is by episode, hashed; by frame it would leak.

run: mirage/validator.py
change: Added the measurement vector and both modes, then ran F-9's threshold sweep. F-2 over all 300,000 frames; the sweep over 8,000 frames drawn from 500 windows.
conclusion: F-2 holds over the WHOLE set, not a sample. Mode 2 is validated directly against ground truth: pixel-only px_count equals the segmentation visible_px exactly on 100% of 6,000 block readings. offpalette_px at tau 8 is the viable verdict expression with 11x headroom. px_count is RULED OUT as a per-frame threshold - the smallest count on a block ground truth calls visible is 1 px with margin 0, because F-7 makes partial occlusion common. Two corrections found by measurement: rgba*255 does not land exactly and not by a modellable rule, so nearest-palette-by-argmin is load-bearing; and the palette needs a 7th entry the XML cannot name - the black void past the table edge is 14.1% of every frame. Thresholds are PRINTED, NOT written into config: the build order recalibrates against Phase 1 tokenizer reconstructions first.

run: bench/hold_probe.py
change: Settled sim.action_hold_steps, a guess since it was written. Settling time by driving one joint from rest and reading the step count at 63% of terminal velocity at four link1 angles; agreement swept over nine holds at 60 episodes x 600 steps; then a gear/damping scaling sweep to test whether the agreement-vs-coverage trade is forced.
conclusion: The ~15-step estimate was wrong: it read dof_armature=0.01 as the inertia, but armature is the term ADDED to the mass-matrix diagonal, not the diagonal. Joint0 takes 21-34 steps depending on link1's angle; joint1 takes 12 and is configuration-independent. The first-order M/b prediction matches every measurement, so both are trustworthy. Two consequences. Q-4's 90% bar is above its own ceiling - ground-truth frames score 83.1% at the shipped hold, so a model reproducing the simulator exactly fails Q-4 by 7 points; that is a requirement defect, not a dataset defect. And no hold satisfies both Q-4 and window coverage at the shipped physics: agreement reaches 90% only at hold 60, where window coverage has fallen from 62.1% to 19.4%. The trade is NOT forced, though - tau = M/damping while v_term = gear*ctrl/damping, so scaling gear and damping together shortens the transient at constant arm speed, and gear 2->6 with damping 0.5->1.5 gives 90.3% agreement at hold 15 with 83.3% coverage. NOT APPLIED: it is a scene edit, so it moves data_hash, invalidates the 300k set and needs F-5, F-6 and F-7 re-verified. action_hold_steps left at 20 pending that decision - now a known trade rather than a guess.

run: PHASE 0 GATE re-run at gear 6 / damping 1.5, action_hold_steps 15
change: Paths B and C from D1/D2 together. Scene scales gear and damping 3x each (2/0.5 -> 6/1.5), which holds terminal velocity at 4.0 rad/s while cutting joint0's settling time from 34 steps to 12; action_hold_steps 20 -> 15; and Q-4 restated from an absolute 90% to 90% of the simulator's own agreement on the same subset. Regenerated all 300k frames at the new data_hash, generated a second time at the same seed for the replay check, then re-ran every M-tier check over the full set.
conclusion: All three gate conditions hold again and every M-tier row re-verified. The two numbers the change was for both moved: Q-4's ground-truth ceiling, measured on the shipped 50/50 mix over 421,701 driven (frame, joint) pairs, is 91.5% against 83.1% before - it now clears the old absolute 90% outright, so the relative restatement is no longer load-bearing for passing, only for honesty; and ctx=15 window coverage is 60.9% against 41.3%, a 1.47x increase in windows carrying any evidence of what an action does. Costs are small and both expected: F-6 fell 20.69% -> 16.63%, still 3.3x its floor, and throughput fell from 6,775 fps because a more responsive arm makes more contacts for the solver to resolve. Scripted-reach arrival ROSE, 36.4% -> 40.0%, which is the same responsiveness helping the reach close. data_hash moved 0259947e -> 219ab0af and validator_hash with it, so every artifact keyed to the old set is unreachable by construction - the hash tree working, not a mess to clean up.

run: E-2 clean build from scratch, sim/build and sim/build-asan
change: Cloned the branch into an empty directory that had never held this project, then ran the documented CMake commands for both build types, ran both binaries, and generated a 40-frame shard with each. E-2 had never been executed - the README's Build section said 'Not yet implemented'.
conclusion: E-2 MET. Both build types configure, compile /W4 /WX clean and run from an empty directory with no manual step beyond the four commands now in README. Three things only a from-empty run shows. (1) The build CANNOT live under %TEMP%: MSBuild's FileTracker fails FTK1011 inside CMake's compiler probe, so it reports as 'no working C++ compiler' rather than as a path problem - this cost the first attempt. (2) sim/build and sim/build-asan keep separate _deps trees, so the second configure re-downloads MuJoCo and re-clones GLFW; nothing is shared and nothing is vendored. (3) The ASan run over the same 40 frames is sanitizer-clean and its .pixels and .meta are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the Release build's, which widens F-4 from 'same build twice' to 'two build configurations' on one toolchain. AND IT FOUND A LIVE PROVENANCE BUG: asked for its data_hash, the clean clone answered 18a76531 where the worktree answered 219ab0af - see the next entry.

run: data_hash CRLF/LF fork, found by the E-2 clean clone
change: Asked the fresh E-2 clone and this worktree, standing on the same commit, for load('mirage/configs/base.json').data_hash. They disagreed. Diagnosed the cause, then normalised CRLF out of the scene XML inside mirage.config.scene_bytes, renormalised 12 worktree files to LF, and regenerated the whole dataset.
conclusion: REFUTES the assumption that .gitattributes closes this. data_hash hashes the scene XML's RAW BYTES, so a CRLF working tree and an LF one name different datasets for one byte-identical scene - the exact fork .gitattributes' own comment says must never happen, live in the repo, with the entire 300,000-frame set stamped 219ab0af, a hash no fresh clone could reproduce. Cause: '* text=auto eol=lf' landed in f0cdf09 and git applies eol only at CHECKOUT - it never rewrites a working tree that already exists, so every file already on disk kept the CRLF core.autocrlf=true had given it. git status hid it, because text=auto normalises before comparing, so the tree read clean. Fixed by normalising inside config.load rather than by trusting the attribute: provenance now depends on nothing a checkout has to honour, and config's self-check asserts a CRLF scene hashes as its LF twin. GENERAL LESSON: a hash over raw file bytes is only reproducible if something normalises those bytes, and 'git handles it' is a convention, not a guarantee. Nothing but a checkout that had never been touched could have surfaced this - every existing tree agreed with itself.

run: PHASE 0 GATE re-run at data_hash 18a76531, with D3's scripted flag
change: Regenerated all 300k frames after the CRLF fix, with D3's is_scripted flag now packed into contact_mask bit 7. Generated a second time at the same seed and SHA256-compared all 14 blobs, then ran both Python self-checks and the ASan build over the writer path.
conclusion: All three gate conditions hold and every M-tier row re-verified. Every measured value is UNCHANGED from the 219ab0af run, which is the expected result: sim/policy.cpp and scene/arm_blocks.xml are untouched (git diff is empty over both), so only the contact_mask byte's high bit differs. F-5 is therefore unchanged by inspection rather than by re-measurement - it is the same computation that read min share 7.17% / ratio 2.15. D3's flag reads correctly: the scripted bit is CONSTANT across every frame of all 500 episodes - asserted per episode, not in aggregate, because a per-frame bug would still leave a plausible mix at the dataset level - and 53.2% of episodes are scripted. That F-6 still reads 16.63% rather than jumping past 50% is the evidence that every reader masks the flag off. The record stays 46 bytes. ASan-clean, both C++ self-checks passing, including the writer check that now alternates the flag and would fail a writer that hardcoded either value.

run: mirage/fixtures - committed self-check fixture, and validator.offpalette_tau
change: Two structural fixes. tau moved out of three validator.py default arguments into validator.offpalette_tau in base.json, read through Config. And a 40-frame fixture - 2 episodes x 20 steps, written by the freshly built mirage_sim.exe from the E-2 run above - committed under mirage/fixtures/, with both self-checks falling back to it when data/shards holds no committed shard.
conclusion: Both self-checks now run in a clone that has never generated anything, which is what F-8's and F-9's acceptance tests being 'python -m mirage.data' and 'python -m mirage.validator' requires - previously both died on FileNotFoundError in every fresh clone, every worktree and any CI. The fixture is real writer output, not synthesised from meta_dtype plus random pixels: F-8 is a claim about the bytes shard_writer.cpp emits, and a synthesised shard would agree with the reader by construction. It costs 4.9 KB packed. Three checks are skipped on the fixture and say so - F-6, F-7, and the episode-level train/val split - because they are claims about the dataset and 40 frames from 2 episodes can only pass or fail them by luck; the split's hash function is instead checked directly over 4,000 synthetic ids, which needs no data at all. VALIDATOR_HASH MOVED, which is the entire point of the tau change: with tau in code, editing it left validator_hash unchanged and two Q-3 coherence-horizon rows taken at different taus would have claimed to be comparable. The VALUE stays uncalibrated until the Phase 1 recalibration - this moved where the number lives, not what it is.

run: bench/occlusion_probe.py
change: Decomposed F-7's occlusion rate over all 300,000 frames into occlusion the block recovers from and a block that never returns, using a reversed cumulative maximum over visible_px per episode. Then projected every block into the camera frustum to say whether the terminal cases had left the table or left the view. No regeneration - the split is recoverable from the shards on disk.
conclusion: REFUTES the recorded cause. The knocked-off-table bias in the checklist's Tier 5 does not exist: NO block has ever left the table, 0 of 900,000 block-frames, worst reach 0.446 m against a 1.2 m half-extent with an arm that reaches 0.33 m. The is_on_table field this project had been reserving for the next regeneration would have separated nothing, and a regeneration is what it would have cost to find that out. The bias itself is real and bigger than the framing implied: 14.48 of F-7's 19.83 points are a block that never returns, so 73% of the headline number is not occlusion. The honest rate is 5.35%, still over the 3% floor but at 1.8x rather than 6.6x - quote that one. The cause is the CAMERA: 12.66% of frames have a block outside the 45-degree frustum, and only 3.56% are terminal with the block still in frame, which is a block parked behind the arm or another block. The projection is validated against the renderer rather than trusted - it agrees on 99.9988% of frames where a block rendered a pixel - and it needs the cube's circumradius as a margin, because blocks reach within 0.196 m of a camera at y=-0.5 and at that range a centre leaves the frustum while a corner is still rendering. A first attempt without that margin disagreed with the renderer on 30% of frames and its own self-check caught it. NO NEW FIELD AND NO REGENERATION: the split falls out of visible_px alone, so Q-6 can score object permanence on occlusion events that actually end, over the shards that already exist. LEFT OPEN: whether F-7's acceptance test should be restated to exclude terminal runs, the way Q-4 was restated once its bar was measured against its own ceiling. That is an M-tier requirement decision, F-7 passes either way, and the numbers are recorded so it can be made on them.

run: F-7 restated - recoverable occlusion only
change: Restated an M-tier requirement on the previous entry's measurement. F-7 now counts only occlusion the block recovers from. Requirement reworded, the validator's acceptance check rewritten to score per episode, the config key renamed occlusion_rate_min -> recoverable_occlusion_rate_min, and the split moved into mirage.data.seen_later so the validator and bench/occlusion_probe.py share one implementation.
conclusion: The bar did not move - the quantity it applies to did. A block reading zero pixels for the rest of an episode is gone, not occluded, and Q-6 cannot score object permanence on an event that never ends; 73% of the old count was exactly that. F-7 passes at 5.35% against the unchanged 3% floor. THE MARGIN IS THE THING TO CARRY FORWARD: 1.8x, not the 6.6x the old number implied, so a scene edit that reduces genuine occlusion has far less room than anyone reading 19.83% would have assumed. THE CONFIG KEY RENAME IS LOAD-BEARING, not cosmetic: the threshold value is unchanged, so without the rename validator_hash would have stayed put while the measurement under it changed meaning, and two incomparable F-7 rows would have claimed to be comparable - the exact failure D9 moved tau into config to prevent. data_hash is untouched, so no regeneration. CROSS-CHECKED: the validator scores per episode over the concatenated shards and the probe scores over a reshaped episode axis, written separately, and they agree at 5.35% to the digit. Precedent for restating a requirement on measurement rather than relaxing it: Q-4, the same week.

run: bench/patch_probe.py
change: Re-measured Phase 1's six pre-work numbers against the current dataset, which is what they were flagged for. The regeneration was not the problem. The original k-means run never recorded its initialisation, and that unrecorded choice is worth 2.4-2.9 dB: random seeding reproduces the old figures to within 0.2 dB, k-means++ seeding beats them by 2.6 dB at 512 centroids. Every init-free statistic - the exact-patch dictionary, the patch entropy, the flat-receptive-field share, the edge-error split - reproduces to within 0.03 dB or 0.4 pp, so the regeneration moved patch statistics almost not at all. The k-means-512 floor is 29.02 dB, not 26.39, so gate row 2's bar is +0.98 dB and not +3.6. All 512 centroids stay live under k-means++, so the stated Q-2 collapse risk was an initialisation artifact too.
conclusion: The six Phase 1 pre-work numbers were re-measured at the current data_hash and the regeneration was exonerated - every init-free statistic reproduced. What moved was k-means, and the cause was an initialisation nobody had recorded: k-means++ beats random seeding by 2.4-2.9 dB. Record the seeding next to the number, always.

run: sim/main.cpp - offwidth/offheight from config
change: Phase 1 build order item 1. The offscreen render size is written into model->vis.global.offwidth/offheight from config between mj_loadXML and the GlContext constructor, so scene/arm_blocks.xml stays byte-identical and a second resolution becomes a config-only change instead of one that rehashes the 64x64 dataset. Proved a no-op at 64x64 by regenerating all 300,000 frames and comparing every blob. Also refuted a claim in the structural plan: the plan said neither existing size check loses its teeth, but main.cpp's viewport cross-check and gl_context.cpp's now compare the same two numbers, so it is one fact checked twice.
conclusion: offwidth and offheight can be written from config without touching the XML: all 300,000 frames regenerated byte-identical and load_shards accepts the result at the same data_hash. A second resolution is now a config-only change. One claim was refuted in passing - the third-corner size check was one fact checked twice, not two.

run: mirage/configs/base96.json - the 96x96 dataset
change: Phase 1 build order item 2. base.json copied with three values changed - sim.height and sim.width to 96, data.shard_dir to data/shards96 - and the set generated. The generation is the first real exercise of item 1's config-driven offwidth/offheight: the context reports a 96x96 viewport off an XML that still says 64. Both self-checks now take an optional config path so a second resolution can be verified without a throwaway script; an explicit path deliberately skips the fixture fallback. Two recorded figures did not reproduce: generation cost and F-7.

The pixel-count extrapolation is refuted as a sizing rule - 2.25x the pixels costs 9% more wall clock, so generation is physics-bound.

run: mirage.data.preload
change: Phase 1 build order item 3. preload returns one split's frames as (n, h, w) uint8 palette indices plus the (7, 3) uint8 LUT that inverts them, rows already flipped top-down. Every predicted figure reproduced exactly: 1.16 GB for the train split at 64x64 against 3.49 raw, 2.62 GB at 96x96 against 7.85, and the same 7-entry LUT at both resolutions. run: mirage/logging.py
change: Phase 1 build order item 4. Run.log(dict) appends one JSON object per line to runs/<run_id>/metrics.jsonl and mirrors to wandb.log only when wandb_project is passed, with a meta.json beside it carrying the git sha, hashes and config. Every record carries the run id and the caller's hashes, so a single line out of the middle of a run identifies which run and which config produced it. Verified with wandb absent from the environment, which is the plan's stated condition, so the W&B mirror is written but UNVERIFIED and marked so in the source. The self-check found one real bug: log() returned the caller's dict rather than the coerced line, so the return value and the bytes on disk could disagree; it now returns the round-trip. It also found that Path coercion via str() emits backslashes on Windows, now as_posix().
conclusion: The jsonl path is verified and the W&B mirror is not, which is exactly the condition the plan names. The self-check found two real bugs in the file it was written for: log() returned the caller's dict rather than the serialised line, and Path coercion emitted backslashes on Windows.

run: mirage/fsq.py 5a-5c, rung R0 - the architecture's ceiling
change: Phase 1 build order item 5, stages 5a (FSQ quantizer), 5b (encoder, GridAttention, decoder) and 5c (MSE + AdamW + cosine, held-out PSNR on uint8). R0 run first and deliberately: continuous bottleneck, quantizer constructed but bypassed, no attention, so the number answers whether this conv stack can reach the 30 dB Q-1 bar at all before any levels table is worth arguing about. It can - 31.228 dB held out, +1.228 over the bar, crossing 30 dB at epoch 6 of 15 and still climbing at 15. codes_to_indices, the R1/R2/R3 ladder and the token cache are NOT written yet, by instruction. 5a's self-check reproduces all three recorded straight-through gradients (0.858 / 1.001 / 0.668) at once, which pins eps, offset, shift and the normalisation simultaneously. TWO REFUTATIONS, and the plan predicted the wrong one. FIRST, attention is a measured non-lever for reconstruction quality: +0.063 dB for +263,680 parameters, a 35% parameter increase returning an eighth of the plan's own within ~0.5 dB means tied threshold. The plan justified GridAttention entirely on PSNR - the attention layer's value shows up in gate row 2, not row 1 - and row 2 is row 1 minus a constant, so it could not have shown up there either. The advantage is small, stable and consistently positive, settling at +0.06 to +0.09 dB from epoch 8 onward rather than decaying, so the effect is real and reproducible and simply an order of magnitude too small to matter. SECOND, and unanticipated by any document, attention IS an entropy lever: +8.2 pp of token entropy and +6 live codes, moving Q-2 from failing by 9.2 pp to failing by 1.0 pp. Joint coding across the grid is a code-utilization mechanism, not a reconstruction one. GridAttention therefore comes off the UNVERIFIED list relabelled: verified as an entropy lever, refuted as a quality lever. That narrows but does not resolve the Q-1/Q-2 collision - the plan's remedy for a Q-2 miss is the shrink ladder [8,8,8]=512 -> [8,6,5]=240, which the held-out floor prices at 1.2 dB of Q-1 headroom (28.27 -> 27.09) on a rung already missing Q-1; against R1's 9.2 pp that was self-defeating, against R2's 1.0 pp it may not be, but nothing yet shows the last 1.0 pp is reachable without it. F.scaled_dot_product_attention reorders its reductions by batch size and ~2 latent values in 100,000 sit close enough to a quantization boundary that the last-bit difference flips the rounded digit. E-1 is satisfiable only with the encode batch pinned, which the manifest now records and evaluate reads. torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True) and the SDPA backend flags were NOT tried, so whether this is avoidable is unmeasured. Row 7 says attention moved none of the edge error - the share went slightly UP, 96.48 -> 96.56% - so what remains is almost entirely edge geometry, which is the 96x96 argument now measured on trained tokenizers. The first half is CONFIRMED at convergence (+0.087 dB for +263,680 parameters); the second half is right in direction but its mechanism was restated by the 2026-08-29 control - attention and training length are substitutes on redundancy, not independent levers. The gate verdict here is an artifact of 15 epochs. The E-1 batch-dependence finding is unaffected and stands: with attention, re-encoding at a different batch changes 10 tokens in 512,000.

change: Not a training run: a computation over the 512-bin counts vector already stored in each rung's tokens/manifest.json, costing no GPU and no re-encode. The mixed-radix id is d0 + 8*d1 + 64*d2, so the three per-channel marginals fall straight out of the counts and the joint entropy splits into the summed marginals minus the redundancy between channels. TWO RESULTS. First, it gives the mechanism behind the unanticipated finding that attention is an entropy lever: 76% of attention's +0.734 bit gain is decorrelation, not better per-channel usage - the summed marginals move only 6.815 -> 6.991 bits while the redundancy falls 1.339 -> 0.781. A layer that lets the 64 cells see each other stops the three FSQ digits carrying redundant copies of the same information, which is exactly what it should do and what no document predicted. R2's channels read 2.432 / 2.595 / 1.964 of 3 bits and the worst puts 81% of its mass on digits 0 and 1, so its pre-quantizer latent sits far off centre in the tanh bound and most of its 8 levels are never reached; R1's third channel is skewed the opposite way, 71.5% on digits 6 and 7, so this is a per-channel offset and scale mismatch and not anything structural. The shrink ladder keeps its mechanism but its diagnosis - the vocabulary collapsed - does not match this miss. The alternative it suggests, centring the latent per channel before the quantizer, is UNMEASURED.

It gave the mechanism behind attention's entropy gain, and it said the Q-2 miss was the wrong shape for the shrink ladder, which fixes collapse where nothing had collapsed. THE INDEPENDENCE INFERENCE DRAWN HERE WAS LATER REFUTED by the fourth cell of the 2x2 - see the R1-at-60 row. The decomposition itself, and the collapse finding, stand.

run: the nn.Upsample mid-frame crash, reproduced on an idle card and diagnosed
change: The crash the 2026-08-28 handoff left as code exonerated, mechanism not, has recurred - and this time the conditions rule out every environmental explanation offered for the first one. R1 at 60 epochs, seed 0, on a card with nothing else on it, five epochs in, died with AttributeError: str object has no attribute align_corners raised inside nn.Upsample.forward. The first occurrence was blamed on contention between two sessions; there was no second session this time. THE DIAGNOSIS, and it is decisive. torch/nn/modules/upsampling.py forward reads self four times in source order: self.size, self.scale_factor, self.mode, self.align_corners. A str has none of those four attributes. Had self been a str on entry to the frame, the failure would have been on self.size at the first access. It failed on the FOURTH. So the frame self slot held a valid Upsample for three bytecodes and a str for the next one, inside a single call, with no assignment to self anywhere in the function. That cannot happen under Python semantics: a bound method self is a fast local that nothing in the frame writes. The object was freed and its memory reused mid-frame, or the frame localsplus slot was overwritten directly - either way a native-layer memory-safety fault, and NOT a bug in fsq.py. The traceback shape is the whole proof and it is cheap to re-check on any future occurrence. WHAT IS RULED OUT. Not contention - the card was idle. Not a CUDA fault - that raises OutOfMemoryError or a CUDA error, not an AttributeError on a CPU-side Python object. Not a free-threading race - sysconfig reports Py_GIL_DISABLED 0 and sys._is_gil_enabled() returns True, so this is a normal GIL build. Not an unsupported Python on paper - torch 2.9.1+cu130 declares Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14 in its own metadata against this 3.14.2. Not a partial import race - the first occurrence already ruled that out by timestamps. WHAT IS NOT RULED OUT, and the next step if it matters enough. The refcounting bug could be in the torch C++ layer, in a CUDA library, or in CPython 3.14 itself, and nothing here separates them. Both occurrences landed in nn.Upsample, which is the only parameterless and bufferless module in the decoder, and both landed during the epoch-boundary eval rather than during training - two patterns worth carrying to a third occurrence rather than trusting at n=2. Running under PYTHONMALLOC=pymalloc_debug would turn the silent reuse into a reported use-after-free at roughly 2x slowdown, and running the same rung on the CPython 3.13.13 available through uv would say whether 3.14 is implicated - neither has been done. THE MITIGATION SHIPPED INSTEAD, because this is not a bug this project can fix: fsq.py now writes a resumable checkpoint every epoch, carrying epoch, optimizer state and the numpy, torch and cuda RNG states, and takes --resume RUN_ID. A crash now costs one epoch instead of the whole run. The RNG states are saved rather than the epoch reseeded on purpose - reseeding per epoch would change the data order and make a resumed rung incomparable to the rungs already measured, which matters when the comparison it exists for is 0.06 dB wide. The crashed run 20260829-004116-r1 predates the resumable format and could not be resumed; it was restarted clean.
conclusion: The crash is a native-layer use-after-free and not a bug in fsq.py, proven by the traceback's shape rather than by reading the project's code: self was valid for three attribute loads and a str for the fourth, inside one frame. Not fixable here, so a resumable per-epoch checkpoint and --resume ship instead, turning a 90-minute loss into a one-epoch loss. Count the attribute accesses before the failing one - that is the technique, and it transfers.

run: mirage/fsq.py rung R1 at 60 epochs - the attention control, and a correction to this session own claim
change: The control run for the attention claim, and it settles two things and refutes a third that this same session had recorded three hours earlier. FIRST, R1 AT CONVERGENCE ALSO PASSES THE WHOLE GATE. 31.095 dB against the 30.0 bar, entropy 74.1% against the 70% bar, rows 4 and 5 clean. So the attention-free 744,966-parameter tokenizer meets item 5 on its own, and GridAttention is not what buys Q-1 or Q-2 - it is not needed for either. SECOND, THE HANDOFF WAS RIGHT ABOUT ATTENTION AND FOR A REASON IT COULD NOT CHECK. Attention buys +0.087 dB at 60 epochs against +0.063 dB at 15 - same order, still about a sixth of the plan within ~0.5 dB means tied threshold, still for +263,680 parameters and a 35% parameter increase. The suspicion that motivated this run - that a 0.063 dB gap measured with both rungs far from converged might have mis-ranked them, which the plan own rule says makes them tied and requiring the long run - was worth acting on and did NOT change the answer. Attention is a measured non-lever for reconstruction quality at convergence too. Matched-epoch deltas stay between +0.05 and +0.11 dB the whole way: +0.052 at epoch 10, +0.105 at 20, +0.066 at 30, +0.094 at 40, +0.087 final. THIRD, AND THIS REFUTES THIS SESSION OWN EARLIER CLAIM. The runs.jsonl row for R2 at 60 epochs and its verification-log row both state that the two entropy deficits have two independent levers - training length cuts marginal skew while leaving redundancy unmoved, attention cuts redundancy while barely touching skew. That was inferred from three cells of a 2x2. The fourth cell, R1 at 60 epochs, refutes the independence: WITHOUT attention, training length cuts redundancy from 1.339 to 0.890 bits. It is not unmoved at all. The full 2x2 in bits, as joint / marginal-sum / skew / redundancy: R1 at 15 is 5.476 / 6.815 / 2.185 / 1.339; R2 at 15 is 6.210 / 6.991 / 2.009 / 0.781; R1 at 60 is 6.670 / 7.560 / 1.440 / 0.890; R2 at 60 is 6.987 / 7.791 / 1.209 / 0.804. THE CORRECTED MECHANISM. On marginal skew the two levers are roughly ADDITIVE and training length dominates: training buys -0.745 bits without attention and -0.800 with it, while attention buys -0.176 at 15 epochs and -0.231 at 60. On redundancy they are SUBSTITUTES, not independent: whichever acts first takes almost the whole reduction and the second adds little. Attention buys -0.558 bits at 15 epochs but only -0.086 at 60; training buys -0.449 without attention but +0.023 with it. R2 at 60 redundancy looking unmoved by training was not evidence of independence - it was evidence that attention had already removed the removable part at 15 epochs and left nothing for training to take. Redundancy floors near 0.78 to 0.89 bits in all four cells, so a structural correlation between the three FSQ channels survives every combination tried and is the part neither lever reaches. WHAT THIS COSTS AND WHAT IT BUYS, for the choice of which checkpoint ships. R1 is smaller by 263,680 parameters, has no E-1 batch-dependence caveat at all (0 tokens differ between encode batches, against 10 in 512,000 for R2), reaches better FLAT PSNR (43.807 against 43.151) and keeps more codes above the 1e-4 mass threshold (485 against 460). R2 is better by +0.087 dB overall, better on edges (27.043 against 26.928), carries 3.5 pp more token entropy (77.6 against 74.1) and puts a smaller share of error on edges (96.00% against 96.63%). Both pass every pass/fail row.
conclusion: Attention is a measured non-lever for reconstruction quality at convergence too - the handoff's verdict survives the control that was run to doubt it. R1 alone passes every gate row, so GridAttention buys neither Q-1 nor Q-2. And the fourth cell of the 2x2 refuted this session's own two-independent-levers claim: the levers are additive on skew and SUBSTITUTES on redundancy, with a 0.78-0.89 bit floor neither reaches. Three cells of a 2x2 supported a clean mechanism the fourth destroyed, and the fourth cost one run.

run: the training step profiled - bf16, TF32, the data path, and the first measurement of run-to-run noise
change: A repo-wide debt and bottleneck audit, run before starting build order item 6. Four measurements, three of which refute something this project had assumed. FIRST, the data path is not the bottleneck and the obvious optimisation is worthless: `_batch` costs 0.47 ms of a 40 ms step, 1.2%, and a pinned staging buffer takes it to 0.20 ms. `non_blocking=True` in `_batch` is a documented no-op on pageable memory and it does not matter. SECOND, `fsq.py`'s train docstring says to add autocast only if a measured step time asks for it; it now asks. bf16 is 1.4-1.5x at 64x64 but only 1.25x at 96x96, because it accelerates the tensor-core matmuls and not the nn.Upsample / GroupNorm / SiLU chain, which is bandwidth-bound, and the bigger image shifts the mix toward the part it cannot help. TF32 alone is 1.07x; cudnn.benchmark is worth nothing at fixed shapes. NOT ADOPTED: R1 and R2 at 60 epochs differ by 0.087 dB and are the comparison item 5 rests on, so changing the arithmetic underneath makes every later rung incomparable to both. Decide it at the 96x96 arm, where a rung costs 3 h, and pay for it by re-running one baseline. AGENDA.md budgets the fork as one config file, ~45 s of generation and one training run; the training run is the part that was never costed. run: --resume was broken on CUDA and had never once been executed
change: Found by writing the first test that ever called the resume path. `train()` loads the checkpoint with `torch.load(map_location=dev)`, which moves EVERY tensor in it to the GPU - the two RNG states included - and `torch.set_rng_state` accepts a CPU ByteTensor only. So the first line of a resume raised `TypeError: RNG state must be a torch.ByteTensor`, on both the torch and the cuda RNG restore. The path was added on 2026-08-29 after the nn.Upsample use-after-free killed two runs, specifically so a mid-flight death would cost one epoch instead of ninety minutes. It was never exercised: the R1 60-epoch rerun `20260829-005439-r1` starts at epoch 0, a fresh run, rather than resuming `20260829-004116-r1` which had just died at epoch 6 - so the machinery built to absorb that crash sat unused while the crash it was built for was being absorbed by hand. Fixed with `.cpu()` on both restores. SEPARATELY, the resume guard checked 7 of the 10 knobs that change the computation: `lr_floor`, `warmup` and `weight_decay` were unchecked though the first two are read by `lr_at` on every step and the third by AdamW, so a resume with a different one silently changed the schedule mid-run while the flag's help text promised 'every knob must match'. Not reachable from the CLI, which exposes none of the three, but `train()` is called directly by anything driving a ladder from Python, which is how R1 and R2 ran. Both fixed and both tested: five cases covering each newly-checked knob, a checkpoint predating them, and a matching resume that must still work; then a sixth that resumes a real 1-epoch checkpoint and requires the remaining epoch to actually train.
conclusion: The crash-recovery path could not survive its own first line, and would have failed at the moment it was finally needed. It now loads, guards all 10 computation knobs, and continues training - 25.66792 dB to 26.51939 dB across the resumed epoch. Reproducibility of a resumed run against an uninterrupted one is NOT claimed: the RNG streams are restored but cuDNN nondeterminism puts a floor of 0.0017 dB under any such comparison anyway.

run: F-9 recalibrated against decoder output - build order item 6
change: The frame validator's palette thresholds were calibrated on MuJoCo renders, where a pixel sits at most 0.75 RGB units from its palette entry and F-9's acceptance condition is literally zero off-palette pixels. Q-3 counts frames out of the FSQ decoder, which emits continuous colour, so the old settings would have fired on frame one of every rollout and the coherence horizon would have read zero forever. New fsq_eval.reconstruction_sweep decodes the whole held-out val split and runs validator.sweep on the result, with the same sweep on the matching ground-truth rows alongside as an alignment assert - it must reproduce F-9's known 0 px / 0.75 dist, otherwise preload's pixels and split_meta's truth are not the same rows. Calibrated on both 60-epoch gate rungs, R2 20260828-230015-r2 and R1 20260829-005439-r1. tau was NOT chosen by the obvious rule of raising it past the worst distance: that needs ~160, a ball 6.5e6 times the calibrated volume, i.e. no palette constraint at all. It was chosen by fixing the threshold at the clean maximum, which is zero false positives by construction, and measuring what fraction of a decayed frame each tau then catches. Decay proxies were a 50/50 blend of two futures (the mush a diverging world model produces), 3x3 and 4x-iterated box blur, gaussian noise sigma 16, and collapse to uniform grey.
conclusion: tau 8.0 -> 32.0 and a new validator.offpalette_px_max of 350. tau 32 is an interior optimum and not a compromise: below it the clean frames have already spent the pixel budget (a clean reconstruction carries off-palette pixels 100% of the time at every tau under 96, so the ground-truth '> 0 px' verdict is unusable), and above it the ball swallows the perturbation - gaussian noise detection falls 100% -> 24.9% -> 0.3% across tau 32/48/64. At tau 32 all five decay proxies are caught at 86.5% or better with zero false positives over 16,200 held-out frames. 350 is 1.11x the 314 px worst clean frame; headroom is expensive here, costing 2.3 points of blend detection and 3.3 of blur, and 512 px would kill blur detection outright at 1.1%, so the margin is deliberately thin and the threshold must not be retuned casually. THREE of the four thresholds the plan expected do not survive measurement and were deliberately not added to config, because a key nothing may read still moves validator_hash: min_visible_px, because a block ground truth calls visible decodes to 0 px; px_count_margin, a diagnostic that was already 0 on renders; and n_unique_max, because blend, blur and grey collapse all come in BELOW the clean maximum of 1,953, so a '>' threshold catches nothing and grey collapse moves the wrong way entirely at 1 unique colour. Ground truth is unaffected at tau 32 - F-2, F-6, F-7 and the 0 px F-9 condition all still hold - so data_hash does not move and the 300,000 frames stay valid. Gate row 6 now runs for real over the whole val split rather than a sample, since the threshold is a maximum and a subsampled gate would be strictly easier than the calibration that set it. Both rungs pass. base96.json carries tau 32.0 and an area-scaled 788 px which is UNVERIFIED - there is no 96x96 tokenizer to calibrate against, and whoever trains one must re-run this.

Motivation is the 96x96 fork: a count is resolution-dependent, so it needs one calibrated value per resolution, and configs/base96.json carried 788 = 350 * 2.25 with no measurement behind it. New bench/palette_pctl_probe.py runs item 6's methodology unchanged - threshold pinned at the max over clean held-out reconstructions (zero false positives by construction), then detection measured against item 6's four decay proxies - but sweeps candidate STATISTICS rather than tau. Candidates: a quantile of per-pixel palette distance at p99/p99.5/p99.9/p99.95, and the off-palette share at the calibrated tau. The chosen bar is 350/4096 exactly, so the 64x64 verdict is bit-identical to item 6's and its calibration is preserved rather than redone.
conclusion: The off-palette SHARE is the verdict; the quantile of distance is REFUTED. The quantile is equally resolution-free and was the candidate this project would have shipped on the argument alone, but it is a tail statistic and the failures that matter are bulk: at the best quantile on the ladder gaussian noise sigma 16 is caught 0.1% of the time against the share's 100%, and above p99.5 every proxy falls to 0% because the zero-FP threshold - a max over 16,200 frames - sits 1.4-1.6x above the median frame. The probe reproduces item 6 independently: clean maxima come back at 298 px (R1) and 314 px (R2), matching r42 exactly. SECOND FINDING, a pre-existing hole rather than a new one: grey collapse is invisible to every palette statistic including the count. A frame collapsed to its own mean lands ~22 RGB units from the table colour, inside tau, so it carries zero off-palette pixels and is palette plausible - r42's 'all five decay proxies are caught' does not hold for this one on the palette check. It is caught by F-9's block-count check, where every block's px_count goes to zero. OPEN, and it is the trigger: the share claims to transfer across resolutions unchanged, and 0.08544921875 * 9216 = 787.5 px - it predicts the very 788 that had no evidence. The edge-localisation argument predicts it will instead come in near 0.667x, about 5.7%, since edge length scales 1.5x where area scales 2.25x. The first 96x96 gate row 6 decides which, and configs/base96.json holds a non-binding 1.0 until it does.

run: The 96x96 arm: R1 at 60 epochs, and the fork priced on a converged tokenizer
change: First 96x96 tokenizer. R1, FSQ [8,8,8], no attention, 60 epochs, batch 128, seed 0 - identical architecture and knobs to the 64x64 R1 gate rung 20260829-005439-r1, so the only variable is resolution and token grid (12x12 = 144 tokens against 8x8 = 64). Killed once at epoch 3 by the nn.Upsample native-layer fault, resumed under a retry wrapper, finished in one further attempt. Gate run against configs/base96.json with the resolution-keyed k-means floor and the resolution-free F-9 share both landed earlier today.
conclusion: THE FORK BUYS Q-1 AND BREAKS Q-2. Row 1 is 32.501 dB against 31.095 at 64x64, +1.406 dB for 2.25x the tokens, on a converged run with every other knob identical - so the 64/144 fork finally has a measured price instead of a prediction. But row 3 reads 55.4% token entropy against the 70% bar, where the same architecture at 64x64 reads 74.1%. THE GATE FAILS AT 96x96. One mechanism explains both signs: an 8x8 patch covers 2.25x less scene at 96x96, so 73.09% of patches are a single flat colour against 63.47%. That is why the held-out k-means floor ROSE to 29.97 dB (easier patches), and it is why the token distribution concentrates. It is skew, not collapse: 0 of 512 codes are unused and 422 carry mass > 1e-4, and the 4.018-bit shortfall is 2.922 marginal skew + 1.096 redundancy against 1.440 + 0.890 at 64x64 - the skew term doubled and the redundancy term barely moved. The Q-2 shrink ladder is therefore triggered for the first time, and it is the right instrument, since it addresses skew. Note the ladder is affordable here in a way it is not at 64x64: 96x96 carries +2.501 dB of Q-1 headroom to spend. SECOND RESULT, and it retires the open trigger from r43: the F-9 off-palette SHARE transfers across resolutions. Clean max is 7.4978% at 96x96 against 7.2754% at 64x64 for the same R1 rung - 1.03x, where the edge-localisation argument predicted 0.667x. The 8.5449% bar therefore serves both resolutions and the 788 px area rescale, which had no evidence when it was written, is correct. THE NUANCE IS WORTH THE ROW: the MEDIAN frame's share is 0.0130 against 0.0183, a ratio of 0.71, which is very nearly the 0.667 the edge argument predicted. So the edge argument is right about the typical frame and wrong about the worst one - and the threshold is a max. A statistic that transfers at the median can still fail to transfer at the tail, and this one happened not to. Row 6 passes at 691 px of the 788 allowed. The quantile candidate stays refuted at this resolution too: noise sigma 16 detection is 0.0%. Cost: 10,574 s of training, 2.94 h, against the 2.80 h predicted - about 4 minutes of that is a double-launch that briefly shared the card, so the prediction holds.

run: DERIVED: pricing the two Q-2 remedies at 96x96 by arithmetic, and the 64/144 fork decision
change: r44 left the 96x96 arm failing gate row 3 at 55.4% against the 70% Q-2 bar. AGENDA names exactly two remedies - the Q-2 shrink ladder ([8,8,8] -> [8,6,5] -> [5,5,5] -> [4,4,4]) and the R2 attention rung - at ~3 h each. bench/entropy_shrink_est.py prices both off the token caches already on disk, training nothing. NOT A MEASUREMENT: two of the three number families are hard bounds and are trustworthy, the third is a coarsening model that holds the latent distribution fixed where a retrained tokenizer would adapt, so it reads pessimistic. No shrunk rung has ever been trained.

attention_ceiling_96.note: sum of marginals - H_joint can never exceed it

conclusion: BOTH REMEDIES ARE REFUTED BEFORE EITHER IS RUN, and one of them model-independently. ATTENTION (option 3) cannot pass, ever: H_joint <= sum of the channel marginals is an identity, that sum at 96x96 is 6.078 bits = 67.5%, and the bar is 70%. Attention drives redundancy toward zero and at EXACTLY zero it still lands at 67.5%. The three transfer estimates off the 64x64 R1 -> R2 measurement give 58.9 / 61.7 / 67.5%, the last being that impossible limit. No run needed. SHRINKING (option 2) fails at the ladder's first step, also model-independently: coarsening can only destroy information, so 4.982 bits / log2(240) = 63.0% is an upper bound for [8,6,5] and it is below the bar. Only [5,5,5]=125 and smaller are even possible, at 71.5% upper bound - 1.5 pp of slack, requiring a shrink that loses essentially nothing, where the coarsening model says it loses 1.64 bits and lands at 47.9%. Best realistic rung is [4,4,4] at 60.9%, still failing. WHY BOTH FAIL IS ONE SENTENCE: 96x96's problem is MARGINAL SKEW (2.922 bits, doubled from 1.440 at 64x64) and not redundancy (1.096, barely moved). The shrink ladder is a collapse fix and there is no collapse - zero of 512 codes unused, 422 live. Attention is a redundancy fix. Neither lever touches skew, and recovering 1.318 of the 2.922 skew bits - 45% of it - is what passing needs. Fixing skew entirely would give 87.8%. Nothing on AGENDA's ladder addresses skew, and the one instrument that would - an entropy auxiliary loss - is explicitly ruled out there, on the grounds that it undoes the reason FSQ was chosen over VQ. That ruling is not revisited here. RECORDED AND NOT ACTED ON: measured against Q-2's stated PURPOSE - that Phase 2 not inherit a smaller vocabulary than it was promised - 96x96 delivers 717.4 bits/frame against 64x64's 426.9, 1.68x, with zero dead codes. The statistic fails while the rationale is satisfied, because tokens are individually less informative when 73.09% of patches are one flat colour, which is a property of the data at that resolution rather than a defect training can remove. This is logged as an observation. THE BAR IS NOT MOVED. Moving a bar because a run missed it is the failure mode this project's evidence discipline exists to prevent, and Q-2 stands as written. DECISION: OPTION 1, ship 64x64. The 64x64 gate passes today on two checkpoints; the 96x96 arm gains +1.406 dB of Q-1 and fails a requirement; and both routes to fixing it are refuted above at a cost of zero GPU hours. With 11 days to the 2026-09-09 deadline and nothing published, a fourth and fifth training run buy a nicer fork table and do not buy a publication. The 96x96 arm is written up AS A RESULT rather than as a failed attempt: the higher-resolution fork buys Q-1 and breaks Q-2, one mechanism drives both signs, and the plan's own two remedies die to arithmetic.

run: Rung r1c: the encoder's spatial normalisation removed, and the locality/entropy trade priced
change: New ChannelNorm in mirage/fsq.py and a new rung r1c in RUNGS. ChannelNorm takes GroupNorm's statistics PER PIXEL rather than over the whole feature map: same GN_GROUPS=8, same learned per-channel scale and shift, same eps, so it carries identical parameters and the rung reports 744,966 - exactly R1's count. The swap is ENCODER ONLY; the decoder keeps GroupNorm throughout, so the only thing that moves is whether a token can depend on pixels its convolutions never touched. Everything else is R1's gate rung exactly: FSQ [8,8,8], no attention, 60 epochs, batch 128, lr 3e-4, seed 0, fp32, data_hash 18a76531 - so the comparison against 20260829-005439-r1 has one variable. encoder_norm is now recorded in the checkpoint knobs, checked by --resume, and read back by fsq_eval.load_run with .get so every pre-existing checkpoint still loads as 'group'. New bench/token_stability_probe.py measures two things off artifacts already on disk, no GPU: token persistence, and P(a token flips GIVEN not one pixel of its own 15x15 convolutional receptive field changed), over 12 held-out episodes. MOTIVATION: an autograd measurement, now asserted in fsq's self-check, that one latent cell's gradient support is the whole 64x64 frame under GroupNorm and exactly 15x15 without it.

wall.note: three segments because the nn.Upsample native-layer fault fired twice, at epochs 22 and 36; --resume carried both seams. Per-epoch wall is 114.6 / 114.6 / 127.1 s and thermal state moves it, so treat it as indicative and not as a comparison against R1's recorded time.

conclusion: LOCALITY IS NEARLY FREE ON Q-1 AND VERY EXPENSIVE ON Q-2, AND THE MECHANISM IS CONFIRMED EXACTLY. The falsifier this rung was run for is a clean zero: with channel-only encoder normalisation, 0 of 396,013 held-out cell-transitions whose own 15x15 receptive field did not change produced a token flip, against 8.86% for R1 and 18.75% for R2. So GroupNorm's spatial statistics were not merely a mechanism that could explain spurious flips, they were the whole cause, and removing them removes the whole effect. The zero is also the probe's own control: an encoder that respects its receptive field is REQUIRED to read exactly 0 here, and a nonzero reading would have condemned the probe rather than the model. Token persistence rises 85.67% -> 93.22%, R2 being worst at 77.28%. THE PRICE IS Q-2 AND IT IS FAR WORSE THAN PREDICTED. The risk recorded before the run was 'about four points of headroom'; the measured cost is 19.5 points, entropy 6.670 -> 4.910 bits, 74.1% -> 54.6% against the 70% bar. GATE ROW 3 FAILS and it is the only failing row. Q-1 costs only 0.282 dB (31.095 -> 30.813) and still passes with +0.813 over the bar and +2.543 over the k-means floor against a +1.73 requirement, so this is not a weaker model - it is the same quality with a differently shaped code distribution. THE SHAPE IS SKEW, NOT COLLAPSE, and it is the 96x96 failure's shape rather than a new one: 0 of 512 codes unused, 463 live at mass > 1e-4 against R1's 485, and the 4.090-bit shortfall splits 2.959 marginal skew + 1.131 redundancy against 1.440 + 0.890 for R1. The skew term doubled and redundancy barely moved - the same signature r45 priced at 96x96, arrived at by a completely different route. That matters for what to do about it: by r45's arithmetic the shrink ladder and attention are redundancy or collapse instruments and neither touches skew, so neither is a candidate remedy here either, and the sum of channel marginals is 6.041 bits = 67.1%, BELOW the 70% bar - so a perfect decorrelator on top of this encoder still fails, model-independently, exactly as at 96x96. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT DO IS DECIDE ANYTHING. It is a control rung, not a gate candidate and not a proposal to replace R1. Q-2's stated purpose is that Phase 2 not inherit a shrunken vocabulary, and unlike the 96x96 arm - which failed the statistic while satisfying the rationale, delivering 1.68x the bits per frame - r1c fails both: 64 tokens x 4.910 bits is FEWER bits per frame than R1's 64 x 6.670, so there is no 'the statistic is measuring the wrong thing' escape available here. NUM-BAR-Q2 is not moved and no checkpoint choice changes on this row. Two collateral results. FIRST, the receptive-field constant: one latent cell's gradient support is 225 px, exactly the 15x15 the three stride-2 3x3 convs give by arithmetic, and 4,096 px - the entire frame - under GroupNorm. bench/patch_probe.py's RF = 22 is neither of those, and 22x22 appears in several documents; the constant is wrong but the direction is safe, since a larger true field means Q-2's derived ceiling had more room than registered, not less. THIS ROW DOES NOT FIX THOSE DOCUMENTS. SECOND, F-11: token persistence is the zero-parameter baseline F-11's 'beat marginal-frequency by 3x' bar has to survive, and at 85.67% for the R1 checkpoint Phase 2 would inherit, it does not - copying the previous frame's token scores far above 3x the marginal top-1. Recorded here as evidence only. WHETHER F-11 IS RESTATED IS A PHASE 2 DECISION AND IS NOT TAKEN HERE. COST: 60 epochs in three segments, 7,175.3 s of training summed, because the nn.Upsample native-layer fault fired twice, at epochs 22 and 36. --resume carried both seams with no visible discontinuity - 30.343 -> 30.381 dB across the first - which is the first time that path has carried a rung to completion rather than merely been tested.

run: Q-5's 10% link-drift bar measured on the simulator's own frames
change: New bench/link_drift_probe.py. No training and no GPU: it reads the shards and mirage.validator only. Q-5 asks a rolled-out world model to hold the arm's link lengths stable across a 200-step rollout, drift <= 10%. In pixels the only available length is the PROJECTED major extent of a link's colour blob, so the probe measures that statistic on GROUND TRUTH frames - the frames a perfect model reproduces exactly - over 12 held-out episodes, 7,200 frames, 36 non-overlapping 200-frame windows per link. Two controls, because a large reading has to be explained or it is indistinguishable from a broken measurement. (1) PROJECTION: the camera's xyaxes are read from scene/arm_blocks.xml rather than hardcoded, giving a world +y compression of 0.403, so a rigid link at world angle theta projects to sqrt(cos^2 + 0.403^2 sin^2) of its face-on length - a 2.48x range from one revolution, with no physics in it. The probe predicts each frame's extent from the meta record's qpos under that model and correlates. (2) VISIBILITY: projection has a FLOOR at 0.403, so extent below it is lost pixels rather than foreshortening. The probe reports the extent-vs-visible-pixel correlation, the share of frames under the floor, and the share whose blob touches the border. This reproduces an unrecorded finding from an earlier session (Q-5's 10% bar fails the simulator's own frames, 35.6% mean) and supersedes that number, which no row ever carried.
conclusion: Q-5 AS WRITTEN IS UNREACHABLE BY ANY MODEL: the simulator's own frames miss its bar by 4.4x on the worse link, 44.2% mean drift against 10%, with 34 of 36 windows over the bar - and 31 of 36 on the better link at 23.0%. A perfect world model, reproducing every frame exactly, fails Q-5. The defect is in the requirement, the same shape as Q-4's ceiling (bench/hold_probe.py, verification log 2026-08-28), and it is NOT a claim that the simulator's links stretch - MuJoCo's links are rigid by construction. BOTH CONTROLS ACCOUNT FOR THE READING, AND THEY NAME DIFFERENT CAUSES FOR THE TWO LINKS, which is what makes this a diagnosis rather than a complaint. link0 is FORESHORTENING and nothing else: r 0.664 against the projection model, min/max 0.458 sitting just above the 0.403 floor the camera geometry predicts, zero frames below the floor, zero clipped. Its 23.0% is the camera, and it would be there on any rigid arm. link1 is VISIBILITY, and the projection model does not merely fail to explain it - the correlation is NEGATIVE, -0.104. Its min/max is 0.097, four times below a floor projection cannot cross, 45.9% of its frames sit under that floor and 32.3% touch the frame border, while the visible-pixel-count correlation is 0.951. The far link passes behind the near one and reaches out of frame; the extent statistic is reading occlusion and clipping. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR PHASE 3: a pixel-space link length is not a measure of rigidity, so Q-5 cannot be accepted on this statistic at any threshold - raising the bar past 44.2% would accept a model that has lost the link entirely, since that is precisely what a 182.6% window is. Either the requirement moves to a quantity that is not projection-and-occlusion bound (the meta record's qpos is available and exact) or it is retired. NOT ACTED ON HERE: this row measures, it does not rewrite Q-5. Moving a bar because a run missed it is the failure mode this project's discipline exists to prevent, and the fact that the run in question is the ground truth is an argument about the STATISTIC, which is a different argument and belongs in the requirements doc with its own decision.

run: Q-3's coherence horizon is blind to dynamics failure: the F-9 substitution probe
change: New bench/q3_blind_probe.py, run against the chosen Phase 2 checkpoint 20260829-005439-r1. Q-3 is frames until the F-9 validator fails, accepted at >= 200. After item 6's recalibration F-9's decoder-output verdict is a PER-FRAME palette-adherence test - off-palette share above validator.offpalette_frac_max at validator.offpalette_tau, here 8.545% at tau 32.0 - and it never compares a frame to a reference. The probe asks whether that verdict can see a dynamics failure AT ALL, without training a dynamics model: take the reconstruction of frame t+300 and offer it as the prediction for frame t. That is the worst dynamics failure available - the arm is somewhere else entirely - while remaining a real decoder output, which is exactly what a well-trained model emits after drifting. 810 pairs over 27 held-out episodes. Frames are round-tripped through the encoder rather than decoded from cached token rows; encoding is deterministic at a pinned batch (gate row 5) so the two are the same frame, and this reuses fsq_eval.reconstruct instead of adding a second decode path. Two controls, because a bare 0.0% is indistinguishable from a broken verdict: the same expression on a sigma-16 noised reconstruction, which bench/palette_pctl_probe.py measured F-9 catching at 100%, and the share of pixels that actually differ between the frame at t and at t+300.
conclusion: F-9 IS BLIND TO DYNAMICS FAILURE, AND SO Q-3'S 200-FRAME HORIZON IS NOT A STATEMENT ABOUT DYNAMICS. The verdict fires on 0.00% of correct reconstructions and on 0.00% of frames taken 300 steps out of position - the same number, to the resolution of 810 pairs. BOTH CONTROLS HOLD, so the reading is the requirement's and not the probe's: the verdict works, catching the sigma-16 noise at 100.00%, and the substituted frames are genuinely wrong, differing on 11.1% of pixels at 17.19 dB - roughly 13 dB below what the tokenizer itself is held to. A model that drifted this far would run out the full horizon and score a PASS. THE MECHANISM IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A THRESHOLD: after item 6 the verdict asks only whether a frame's colours are on the palette, and a decoder trained on this dataset emits palette colours for ANY plausible arm pose, correct or not. Nothing in the expression references frame t, so no value of tau or offpalette_frac_max can recover a comparison the statistic does not make. This does NOT invalidate item 6 or F-9 itself, which is a per-frame plausibility check and does the job it claims - F-9 catches a decoder that has stopped producing valid frames, and it still catches it here. It invalidates the INFERENCE Q-3 draws from it, that surviving 200 F-9 verdicts means the rollout stayed coherent. WHAT PHASE 3 NEEDS instead is a termination test that sees position: the arm-pose and block-count halves of F-9's own wording are candidates and neither is implemented, and a reference-comparing measure is available for a teacher-forced rollout though not for a free one. UNMEASURED AND DELIBERATELY SO: no shorter lag was swept. A lag sweep would price how wrong a frame must be before F-9 notices, but 0.00% at the worst available failure already answers the question that was asked, and a sweep would answer a different one.

run: Phase 2 dynamics model sized and its epoch priced, four parameter variants
change: New bench/dyn_size_probe.py. NOT A PHASE 2 DECISION: it prices the model the docs already specify (world_model_ingredients.md - d_model 384, 8 layers, 6 heads, plain MHA - and configs/base.json dynamics), so the Phase 2 structural plan can be written against numbers rather than against recollections computed in an earlier session and never written down. Context is 15 frames x (64 tokens + 1) = 975 positions, vocab 521 in and 512 out. FOUR VARIANTS ON PURPOSE: the parameter count depends on two choices docs/handoff_tokenizer_decision.md section 7 decision 4 calls irreversible - sequence layout and position encoding - so the table prices tied against untied output embeddings and RoPE against learned positions rather than quoting one number and deciding by accident. Throughput is MEASURED at batch 16 rather than modelled, because that is what an estimate gets wrong: fp32 matmul here does not use TF32 by default and thermal state moves the answer. bench/gpu_probe.py was run alongside and its verdict is recorded below.
conclusion: THE MODEL IS ~14.4-15.0 M PARAMETERS and the spread across the four variants is 571,008 - under 4% - so the irreversible layout choice is NOT a capacity choice and can be made on its merits. bf16 is the only sane precision: 221.6 ms/step against fp32's 622.4, 2.81x, for 1.06 h/epoch against 2.99 h. THE THROUGHPUT NUMBERS ARE A LOWER BOUND AND MUST NOT BE QUOTED AS THE MACHINE'S CAPABILITY: gpu_probe returned compute FAIL for this session - the SMs held 2385 MHz of a 3090 MHz maximum and fp16 matmul read 20.6 TFLOP/s where this machine has recorded 27.6 after the chassis cooling fix - so a clocked-up run is faster by up to ~34% and 1.06 h/epoch is the pessimistic figure. Re-measure before any schedule depends on the margin. THE FINDING THAT MATTERS FOR THE PLAN IS THE DATA, NOT THE COMPUTE: 19.5 M tokens against a Chinchilla-optimal 291.9 M for this parameter count is 15.0x under, so Phase 2 is DATA-BOUND AND NOT COMPUTE-BOUND, and the token cache carrying all of it is 38.4 MB - it fits in VRAM many times over, so nothing about the data path needs engineering. One epoch draws 276,705 overlapping windows totalling 269.8 M tokens, which exceeds the dataset 13.8x from overlap alone; that is repetition, not new information, and it means the risk to manage in Phase 2 is overfitting rather than throughput. NOT DECIDED HERE: whether to answer the shortfall with more data, a smaller model, or heavier regularisation. All three are open, and this row only prices the gap.

run: The restated Q-5 statistic - deprojected, visibility-filtered - and its refutation
change: bench/link_drift_probe.py extended with the repair r47's two controls implied. r47 showed the raw statistic fails on ground truth for two removable-looking reasons - camera foreshortening on link0, occlusion and clipping on link1 - so this run removes both and re-reads. DEPROJECTION uses the PIXEL-MEASURED link_angle and never qpos, which is the whole constraint: a model's rollout has no ground truth to consult, so a correction needing qpos cannot be applied to the thing Q-5 scores. An image direction (cos phi, sin phi) comes from a world direction proportional to (cos phi, sin phi / k) with k = 0.403 read from the camera's own xyaxes, and the factor is that direction's projected length once normalised - no branch at phi = pi/2, and sign never enters, so neither image y running downward nor PCA's undefined eigenvector sign matters. VISIBILITY FILTER excludes frames whose blob touches the frame border or whose px_count falls under tol * area_ref * factor, where area_ref is the 99th percentile of px_count / factor - a rigid link's blob area foreshortens by the same factor its length does, so that ratio is flat while the link is whole. tol is SWEPT over 0.70 / 0.80 / 0.90 rather than picked, because a single value tuned until ground truth passes would be the circular argument the probe exists to avoid. Windows keeping fewer than 50 of their 200 frames are dropped rather than scored. One control on the deprojection itself: the pixel-derived factor against the qpos-derived one. The raw path is untouched and reproduces r47 exactly. Also fixes a latent shadowing bug - the window loop reused w, the frame width, which was harmless only because nothing read it afterwards.
conclusion: THE REPAIR FAILS, AND THE DRAFTED Q-5 RESTATEMENT IS REFUTED BEFORE IT REACHED THE DOC. Deprojecting and excluding non-visible frames leaves 25.9% to 34.8% drift against a 10% bar - a factor of 2.6 to 3.5 out, where the raw statistic was 2.3 to 4.4 out. It buys nothing at any tolerance on the sweep. THE DEPROJECTION IS NOT WHAT FAILED: its control passes on link0 at r 0.928 against the qpos-derived factor, so the angle convention and the camera model are right. link1's 0.613 is the expected consequence of measuring an angle on a blob that is occluded or clipped half the time, and it is the link the filter then discards. SO THE RESIDUAL IS NEITHER FORESHORTENING NOR CLIPPING - both were removed and it barely moved. What is left is the noise floor of a PCA major extent taken on a blob of roughly 30 pixels at 64x64, where one boundary pixel is several percent of the length and the (max - min) / median window statistic is a RANGE, so a single bad frame sets it. That floor is a property of the resolution and of pixel-space measurement, not of the requirement's wording, and no restatement removes it. THE FILTER'S OWN COST CONDEMNS THE APPROACH INDEPENDENTLY: it keeps 23.3% of link0's frames at the loosest tolerance and 3.9% of link1's, dropping 25 of 36 and 35 of 36 windows. link1 scores ZERO windows at both tighter tolerances. A requirement that discards 96% of the rollout it is meant to police is not a requirement. WHAT THIS LEAVES is the fallback the draft named before the run: Q-4's precedent, a bar stated RELATIVE to the simulator's own reading on the same statistic over the same subset, with both numbers reported. It applies to the RAW statistic - r47's 23.0% and 44.2% - because deprojection has now been measured to buy nothing, and keeping it would add two knobs and a discarded-frame problem for no gain. NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY: no search for a third statistic that ground truth happens to pass. A robust spread such as an interquartile range over the median would very likely pass, and would have been chosen for exactly that reason, which is the circularity this row and its tol sweep exist to refuse. RECORDED AS A NEGATIVE RESULT so nobody re-attempts the deprojection: the code stays in the probe, marked refuted in its docstring.
